sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: newcomer rules, retest fees, card types, document rules and road test details
Confusable pairs from the first half of chapter one, followed by continuation facts on enhanced cards, name changes, translations, special licenses and road test details; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
A newcomer from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada can skip the written and road tests with a valid license, but a newcomer from any other country takes all three tests even with a valid foreign license. [A01]
Why it matters: group newcomers; confusable U.S. or Canada versus other countries; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
The newcomer deadline is 60 days for a regular license but only 30 days for a commercial license after becoming a Minnesota resident. [A01]
Why it matters: group newcomers; confusable regular versus commercial deadline.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
A visiting nonresident needs to be only 15 with a valid home license, but the no-license exception for drivers from countries that do not license drivers requires age 18 and is capped at 90 days per calendar year. [A01]
Why it matters: group exemptions; confusable two nonresident exceptions; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A05
A failed written test series costs $10 per attempt starting with the third, while the road test retest fee on the next pages is a different amount. [A05]
Why it matters: group retest fees; confusable written versus road retest fee.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A07
The road test retest fee is $20 for each attempt after two failures, double the written test retest fee. [A07]
Why it matters: group retest fees; confusable written versus road retest fee.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A05
Central vision must reach 20/40 and side vision must reach 105 degrees; falling short of the side-vision number alone is enough to be referred to an eye doctor. [A05]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable central versus peripheral standard.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A03
A photo Minnesota card can serve as identification up to five years after expiry, but a card without a photo only up to one year after expiry. [A03]
Why it matters: group identification; confusable photo versus non-photo card; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A03
A standard card under the Driver's License for All law needs no proof of legal presence, while a REAL ID card requires a document proving legal presence and two residency documents. [A03]
Why it matters: group card types; confusable standard versus REAL ID.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A03
An enhanced license or ID is limited to U.S. citizens who prove identity, full legal name, Social Security number, photo identity and Minnesota residency, and the card must show the Minnesota residence address. [A03]
Why it matters: group card types; confusable REAL ID versus enhanced.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A03
An enhanced card applicant gives two kinds of residency proof, completes an interview questionnaire, and pays a $15 fee on top of the regular license or ID fee. [A03]
Why it matters: group card types; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A02
No Minnesota license is needed to drive a farm tractor or farm implement temporarily on a public road, to operate a snowmobile, or to run a locomotive or other on-track rail equipment. [A02]
Why it matters: group exemptions; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A04
A legal name change through marriage, divorce or court order is proved with a certified marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order naming the change, and every change in a series must be documented. [A04]
Why it matters: group documents; prereq identification rules.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A04
A document not in English needs a qualified English translation whose translator certifies it is full and accurate, that they are competent in both languages, that they are not related to the subject by blood or marriage, and that a false translation carries a penalty. [A04]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A04
A person serving more than six months in a jail or correctional facility without an existing DVS agreement can renew a license or ID by mail. [A04]
Why it matters: group special licenses; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A04
A reintegration license for someone released from a Minnesota prison is temporary, expires 15 months after it is issued, and is canceled if the holder breaks traffic laws and loses driving privileges. [A04]
Why it matters: group special licenses; confusable reintegration versus regular license.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A06
Equipment required by your license or permit restrictions must work for the road test unless you are testing to remove those restrictions. [A06]
Why it matters: group road test vehicle; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A06
On a vehicle with fully automatic headlights, the driver must still switch the high and low beams on manually during the equipment check. [A06]
Why it matters: group road test vehicle; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A07
After passing the road test, an applicant under 18 needs the application signed by a parent, a legal guardian, a foster parent appointed by a county, or the director of the transitional living program where they live. [A07]
Why it matters: group under eighteen; prereq parental approval rules.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A07
Giving false medical information on a permit or license application can cost you your driving privileges, and a medical condition may require a physician's statement on whether it affects safe driving. [A07]
Why it matters: group medical; confusable new diagnosis deadline versus application questions.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0015]
